div.div:
Paths
/worker/v1, signed object URLs and /state/v1 all use the tunnel host. cloudflared forwards to the HTTPS front, which balances over servers A and B; the servers sign object URLs with the tunnel origin.

text.tspan: /worker/v1, signed object URLs and /state/v1 all use the tunnel host.
cloudflared forwards to the HTTPS front, which balances over servers A
and B; the servers sign object URLs with the tunnel origin.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 357px; height: 1px; padding-top: 849px; margin-left: 399px;

div.div:
Trust anchors and egress
Pods trust system roots: Cloudflare's certificate on the tunnel host. cloudflared trusts the front's CA. Pods need outbound 443 through each cloud's NAT; the runner needs only outbound connections.

text.tspan: Pods trust system roots: Cloudflare's certificate on the tunnel host.
cloudflared trusts the front's CA. Pods need outbound 443 through each
cloud's NAT; the runner needs only outbound connections.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 357px; height: 1px; padding-top: 849px; margin-left: 788px;

div.div:
For
No server stack in any cloud. The platform, its coverage and its cleanup stay on the runner like every other lab batch. Smallest scope and cost.

text.tspan: No server stack in any cloud. The platform, its coverage and its cleanup
stay on the runner like every other lab batch. Smallest scope and cost.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 357px; height: 1px; padding-top: 849px; margin-left: 1177px;

div.div:
Against
Every Pod request crosses Cloudflare and the runner's uplink. A quick tunnel has no SLA and a new host each run; a named tunnel adds an account, a domain and a token secret. The control plane is public for the run.
